words.technical: Gold rose about 4.6% on the week, but the longer trend readings are still negative: the 63-day and 126-day trend measures sit near -0.76 and -0.91, and the combined trend score is -0.47. Price sits in the bottom eighth of its 252-day range, so this is a bounce inside a downtrend rather than a confirmed reversal. Daily volatility of roughly 1.5% keeps the one-week range wide.
words.macro: Gold's rebound off last Friday's 13-month closing low narrowed from 7.0% to 4.1% at $4050 per troy ounce by Friday afternoon. The US jobs report pushed the unemployment rate down to 4.1%.
words.long_term: The 252-day trend is still marginally positive while everything shorter is negative, so the structural picture is a pullback within a larger advance that has not yet shown it is over.

eoy_scenarios.central: Gold stays inside the middle of its range, with the bounce from the lows holding but no decisive trend returning as inflation and jobs data trade off against each other.
eoy_scenarios.upside: A softer inflation print and a weaker dollar extend the rebound, pulling price back toward the top of the recent range and turning the shorter trend measures upward.
eoy_scenarios.downside: Strong labour data and a firmer dollar push rate-cut expectations out, and the recent low gives way as the downtrend resumes.

words.long_term: Silver trades as a higher-volatility cousin of gold; the long-window trend is barely positive and the structural picture depends on whether the 2026 low holds.

eoy_scenarios.downside: Weak industrial demand and a stronger dollar send silver back to retest and break the recent low.

words.long_term: The dollar has been in a steady advance and is trading near the top of its one-year range, so the structural picture is strength that is already well established.

week_summary: A violent week for risk assets: the Nasdaq 100 fell nearly 5% and the S&P 500 lost about 2.7%, oil dropped more than 13%, and gold and silver bounced hard off multi-month lows. The dollar firmed slightly and Bitcoin slipped. The stances for the week ahead are mostly cautious or range-bound, with US inflation data due on 10 November the next scheduled test.
